parsed.study_design: Cross-sectional hedonic price analysis of nationally representative household survey data
parsed.population_and_sample: 12,476 urban and rural homeowner households from Guatemala's 2006 Living Standards Measurement Survey (ENCOVI), comprising 4,810 urban and 7,666 rural households
parsed.exposure: Household water-source access and service-governance arrangement, including in-house and yard connections supplied by municipal, private, or community-managed utilities; public taps, wells, other sources, source distance, and service unreliability were also examined
parsed.outcome: Households' economic valuation of water access, estimated through stated monthly rental prices and marginal values of water connections; service reliability and source distance were secondary access-related outcomes/explanatory measures
parsed.rationale: Section 3 (pp. 21–24) identifies the population, nationally representative ENCOVI sample, water-access and governance exposures, stated-rent outcome, and fixed-effects hedonic design. Results in Tables 5–7 (pp. 25–28) empirically estimate how municipal, private, and community-managed provision, connection type, source distance, and unreliability relate to household valuation of water access. The paper therefore directly examines household water-service access under distinct institutional governance arrangements and reports extractable access-relevant outcomes.
